key_insight: Instead of re-deriving control logic in every prompt, the paper grows a reusable agent harness from task feedback so repeated decisions become executable code.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for building lower-cost, more scalable LLM agents that preserve performance by shifting recurring orchestration from context to persistent software.
method: Start from a strategy-free scaffold with fixed model and tool interfaces.
Localize failures with function-level execution traces and repair a bounded code window jointly.
Use a success-first held-out gate to roll back edits that reduce prior capability, then accumulate accepted changes in one shared harness.
evidence_signal: Across BrowseComp-Plus and WebArena-Verified with 4B to 120B deployment models, Growing Harness achieved the best mean success in 5 of 6 settings and cut LLM calls by 76.0–91.8%.
watch_item: Because the harness evolves over time, careful rollback, trace quality, and evaluation gating are important to avoid regressions or overfitting to a benchmark task mix.
paper_title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
